findings.title: JWT issuer validation bypass via array `iss` loose match
findings.evidence: The `iss` validator is registered without any scalar-only guard (src/verifier.js:474-476) even though `iss` must be a single string everywhere else in the library (signer.js:270-271 enforces `typeof iss === 'string'`; index.d.ts:108 types it as `string`; only `aud` is declared array-capable at src/verifier.js:470-472). In verifyToken the raw claim is used without rejecting arrays: `const value = payload[claim]` (line 210), `const arrayValue = Array.isArray(value)` (line 211), `const values = arrayValue ? value : [value]` (line 212). `validateClaimType` (lines 144-152) only checks `typeof` of each element, so an array of strings passes the type check, and `validateClaimValues` then matches with ANY semantics: `if (!values.some(v => allowed.some(a => a.test(v))))` (line 159). An attacker who supplies a signature-valid token whose payload contains `iss: ["<allowed-issuer>", "<attacker-value>"]` therefore passes the `allowedIss` check as long as exactly one array element matches, instead of being required to present a single string `iss`. The same omission applies to `jti`/`sub`/`nonce`. The array is attacker-controlled payload data and reaches the loose comparison via verifier(token) -> decode -> verifyToken -> validators loop (lines 209-227) -> validateClaimValues; the only precondition is that the token passes signature verification (or the deployment explicitly allows `alg: none`), so no array/scalar type guard protects the sink.
